Resolve problems in a sound, logical and decisive manner.

competencies.competency: Project Management
competencies.description: Project Management in the context of data science involves planning, organizing, and overseeing data-driven projects from initiation to completion. It includes managing resources, timelines, and deliverables while ensuring that project goals align with business objectives. It also involves risk management, stakeholder communication, and iterative problem-solving throughout the project lifecycle.
indicators: Assist in planning project tasks and timelines, and ensure milestones are met under direct supervision.
Help allocate resources (time, people, tools) for simple tasks or project phases.
Understand and follow project timelines and task lists.
Identify simple project risks, such as timeline delays or resource shortages, and raise awareness with the team.
Contribute to maintaining project documentation (e.g., status reports, project timelines) and keep records updated.

competencies.competency: Artificial Intelligence Techniques
competencies.description: The Artificial Intelligence Techniques competency encompasses the knowledge and skills required to develop, deploy, and manage AI-driven solutions, including machine learning algorithms, deep learning models, natural language processing (NLP), and generative AI systems. It covers the full AI pipeline from data preparation and model development to ethical considerations and model deployment.
indicators: Apply basic machine learning algorithms, including supervised and unsupervised techniques.
Define core AI concepts, such as machine learning, deep learning, large language models, and vision-language models.
Use open-source libraries to build basic models.
Perform effective prompt engineering.
Evaluate the quality of LLM's.

competencies.competency: Thinking Things Through (Create Vision and Strategy)
competencies.description: Thinking Things Through is the ability to systematically analyze problems, identify patterns and connections, and develop well-informed plans and recommendations. This competency involves asking the right questions, evaluating cause and effect relationships, and turning analysis into clear strategies that align with organizational goals.
indicators: Inform analysis with a thorough understanding of the environment.
Translate implementation strategies, objectives and direction into concrete activities.
Contribute expertise and insight to the development and implementation of organizational strategies.
Communicate with clarity and conviction.
Respond to changes in direction and organizational priorities.
Design and implement solutions to operational challenges.

title: CSPS Digital Accelerator Learning Path
description: This learning path offers a self-directed journey through a selection of learning tools (courses, articles, videos, job aids) that support collaborative and user-centred design and delivery on topics such as digital, design, agile, product and service management, qualitative data synthesis, and more.

competencies.competency: Working Effectively with Others (Mobilize People; Collaborate with Partners and Stakeholders)
competencies.description: Working Effectively with Others is the ability to build strong, collaborative relationships within and outside the organization. It involves sharing information openly, encouraging diverse viewpoints, and enabling teamwork to solve problems and achieve shared goals. This competency extends to supporting others through change, providing constructive feedback, mobilizing teams around a common purpose, and fostering partnerships that amplify organizational effectiveness.
indicators: Share relevant information to facilitate collaboration.
Accomplish independent tasks as part of one's own share of the work.
Work with others to clearly define problems and identify suitable solutions.
Suggest methods and means for maximizing the input and involvement of team members.
Facilitate the expression of diverse points of view to enhance teamwork.
Openly share data/findings to support other teams' work.

competencies.competency: Project Management
competencies.description: Project Management in the context of data science involves planning, organizing, and overseeing data-driven projects from initiation to completion. It includes managing resources, timelines, and deliverables while ensuring that project goals align with business objectives. It also involves risk management, stakeholder communication, and iterative problem-solving throughout the project lifecycle.
indicators: Assist in planning project tasks and timelines, and ensure milestones are met under direct supervision.
Help allocate resources (time, people, tools) for simple tasks or project phases.
Understand and follow project timelines and task lists.
Identify simple project risks, such as timeline delays or resource shortages, and raise awareness with the team.
Contribute to maintaining project documentation (e.g., status reports, project timelines) and keep records updated.

title: Crisis of Confidence: A Digital Solution
description: This video features Scott Brison in his former role as the President of the Treasury Board and Minister of Digital Government describing how the Government of Canada can strengthen its relationship of trust with Canadians by offering more effective and modern services.

competencies.competency: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
competencies.description: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect is the commitment to ethical behavior, transparency, and fairness in all professional actions. This competency involves consistently adhering to organizational values, ethical guidelines, and legal standards especially when handling sensitive data or implementing analytical methods. It encompasses identifying, discussing, and mitigating ethical risks, supporting colleagues in ethical decision-making, and ensuring practices such as privacy protection, bias reduction, and inclusion are upheld throughout all processes.
indicators: Comply with the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector in all aspects of data/AI use.
Discuss ethical concerns with appropriate individuals or channels and seek guidance for ethical/privacy issues.
Identify and report ethical concerns when appropriate.
Adhere to the organization's legal, privacy and ethical frameworks (Privacy Act, Policy on Privacy Protection, etc.) and follow disclosure procedures.
Identify and proactively flag privacy/security/accessibility implications.
Consult responsible AI resources.
Consult key policies/procedures on AI for decision-making.
Ensure privacy/security is set at the right permission levels.

competencies.competency: Business Acumen
competencies.description: Business acumen in data science refers to the ability to understand and apply knowledge of business operations, strategy, and decision-making processes. It involves identifying business needs, aligning data-driven insights with organizational goals, and making decisions that drive organizational success.
indicators: Demonstrate basic understanding of key business functions, such as marketing, finance, and operations, and how they relate to data science projects.
Recognize business problems and basic opportunities where data analysis can contribute to business goals.
Understand key financial metrics (e.g., revenue, profit margins, cost structures) and how they impact business decisions.
Present data findings in simple terms, ensuring they are relevant and understandable for business stakeholders.
Recognize various data types and value as an organizational asset.

title: Respecting Gender Identity in the Workplace
description:
Description

Understanding and respecting gender diversity is essential for fostering inclusivity and a sense of belonging. This online self-paced micro-course begins with a short video, followed by reflection questions and resources that encourage learners to examine their assumptions, develop respectful practices, and navigate sensitive situations with empathy and care. Participants will learn strategies to create more supportive and respectful professional environments by building awareness of the nuances of gender identity and avoiding common mistakes.

Topics include:

- understanding the impacts of deadnaming and misgendering
- identifying inclusive behaviours
- responding to mistakes regarding gender identity
- demonstrating active allyship

title: Recognizing the Impacts of Systemic Anti-Black Racism in the Workplace
description:
Description

Anti-Black racism remains a systemic issue in many workplaces. This online self-paced micro-course begins with a short video scenario depicting a Black public servant’s experience with systemic racism and its impacts, followed by reflection questions and resources. Participants will gain a deeper understanding of how systemic racism can affect career advancement and the mental and physical health of Black employees.

Topics include:

- understanding the barriers to career progression
- addressing discrimination and exclusion
- identifying the psychological impacts of systemic racism
- demonstrating active allyship

competencies.competency: Technical Communication
competencies.description: Technical communication is the ability to effectively convey complex data and analytical insights to diverse audiences, ensuring clarity, accuracy, and relevance. This competency encompasses presenting information using appropriate visual and narrative techniques, adapting messaging to suit stakeholder needs, and linking data findings to organizational objectives. Strong technical communicators make data accessible and actionable, bridging the gap between technical analysis and business decision-making. Mastery of this skill empowers teams to drive informed strategies and foster collaboration across the organization.
indicators: Present basic data analysis results in clear, simple terms using basic charts and graphs (e.g., bar charts, line plots), ensuring key insights are understandable to technical and non-technical audiences.
Summarize the findings of simple analyses (e.g., descriptive statistics or basic trends) in a straightforward manner. Focus on clarity and conciseness.
Use basic visual tools (e.g., Excel charts, basic Python/R plotting) to represent data in ways that make trends and relationships easy to understand.
Use appropriate data/AI terms and concepts when communicating.
Cite sources of information/AI-generated content in visuals.

title: Recognizing Microaggressions Towards Indigenous People
description:
Subtle comments or behaviours, even when unintentional, can cause harm in the workplace by creating an environment where individuals feel excluded or undervalued. This micro-course introduces the concept of microaggressions towards Indigenous people and offers practical strategies to recognize and address them. Participants will deepen their understanding of microaggressions and learn how to help create a more inclusive and respectful work environment.

 

Topics include:

 

- defining microaggressions
- identifying common microaggressions experienced by Indigenous people
- acknowledging the impacts of microaggressions through a video case study
- responding respectfully when microaggressions occur

title: Finding Health Equity for First Nations Children
description: Everyone should have the opportunity to attain their full health potential. Avoidable, unfair or remediable differences in opportunity, whether they be social, economic, demographic or geographic, are a sign of an unacceptable inequity among groups of people. In its 2016 ruling, the Canadian Human Rights Tribunal found that First Nations children were being discriminated against as a result of the inequitable funding of child and family services. In this video, Dr. Cindy Blackstock, Ph.D., Executive Director of the First Nations Child and Family Caring Society of Canada, and Professor Sir Michael Marmot, Director of the International Institute for Society and Health, discuss the pursuit of equity for First Nations children in the context of Jordan's Principle and the Pan American Health Organization's recent report Just Societies: Health Equity and Dignified Lives.

competencies.competency: Technical Communication
competencies.description: Technical communication is the ability to effectively convey complex data and analytical insights to diverse audiences, ensuring clarity, accuracy, and relevance. This competency encompasses presenting information using appropriate visual and narrative techniques, adapting messaging to suit stakeholder needs, and linking data findings to organizational objectives. Strong technical communicators make data accessible and actionable, bridging the gap between technical analysis and business decision-making. Mastery of this skill empowers teams to drive informed strategies and foster collaboration across the organization.
indicators: Present basic data analysis results in clear, simple terms using basic charts and graphs (e.g., bar charts, line plots), ensuring key insights are understandable to technical and non-technical audiences.
Summarize the findings of simple analyses (e.g., descriptive statistics or basic trends) in a straightforward manner. Focus on clarity and conciseness.
Use basic visual tools (e.g., Excel charts, basic Python/R plotting) to represent data in ways that make trends and relationships easy to understand.
Use appropriate data/AI terms and concepts when communicating.
Cite sources of information/AI-generated content in visuals.

competencies.competency: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
competencies.description: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect is the commitment to ethical behavior, transparency, and fairness in all professional actions. This competency involves consistently adhering to organizational values, ethical guidelines, and legal standards especially when handling sensitive data or implementing analytical methods. It encompasses identifying, discussing, and mitigating ethical risks, supporting colleagues in ethical decision-making, and ensuring practices such as privacy protection, bias reduction, and inclusion are upheld throughout all processes.
indicators: Ensure that standards and safeguards are in place to protect organizational integrity.
Champion the integration of AI governance frameworks, including human-in-the-loop oversight and transparency protocols.
Develop and enforce ethical review protocols for AI projects, ensuring alignment with TBS and StatCan guidelines.
Guide teams in applying fairness review checklists and employment equity principles in AI-supported processes.
Engage stakeholders to ensure inclusive design strategies that accommodate and benefit from differences between groups.
Lead the implementation of Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) and Algorithmic Impact Assessments (AIAs) for high impact AI.
Design and implement policies/processes for ethical approaches to research/data use.
Promote responsible/ethical use of AI as an organizational norm.
Champion open data/transparency.

title: Project Management Learning Path: Level 1 – Working-Level Fundamentals
description:
Project management plays an essential role in supporting government initiatives of all sizes. Level 1 of the Project Management Learning Path introduces Foundational project management principles, tools, and practices in a public sector context. Participants will gain the skills to contribute meaningfully to project teams and navigate planning, risk, and scheduling activities.


Topics include:

·       applying core project management roles, terminology, and concepts

·       using essential tools for defining scope, planning, and scheduling

·       contributing to risk identification and stakeholder analysis

·       supporting collaboration in virtual and hybrid team settings

·       recognizing the impact of organizational change on project delivery

title: Project Management Learning Path: Level 2 – Becoming a Practitioner
description:

competencies.competency: Business Acumen
competencies.description: Business acumen in data science refers to the ability to understand and apply knowledge of business operations, strategy, and decision-making processes. It involves identifying business needs, aligning data-driven insights with organizational goals, and making decisions that drive organizational success.
indicators: Head the creation of data-driven business models that optimize profitability, revenue generation, or customer engagement. Ensure alignment with long-term business strategy.
Guide senior Leadership on strategic decisions based on data insights, providing recommendations that align with both short- and long-term business goals.
Champion the integration of data-driven decision-making across all business functions, promoting a culture of data-driven Leadership.
Manage cross-functional teams to ensure data-driven projects meet organizational goals and generate measurable business value.
Head innovation initiatives that leverage data science to transform business processes, create new revenue streams, or disrupt the market.
Help others translate organizational needs/mandate into data/AI requirements for projects.
Apply governance in specific operational business contexts (e.g., obtaining policy guideline approval).
Define and implement strategies for advancing organizational AI talent, systems, and infrastructure.

competencies.competency: Working Effectively with Others (Mobilize People; Collaborate with Partners and Stakeholders)
competencies.description: Working Effectively with Others is the ability to build strong, collaborative relationships within and outside the organization. It involves sharing information openly, encouraging diverse viewpoints, and enabling teamwork to solve problems and achieve shared goals. This competency extends to supporting others through change, providing constructive feedback, mobilizing teams around a common purpose, and fostering partnerships that amplify organizational effectiveness.
indicators: Share relevant information to facilitate collaboration.
Accomplish independent tasks as part of one's own share of the work.
Work with others to clearly define problems and identify suitable solutions.
Suggest methods and means for maximizing the input and involvement of team members.
Facilitate the expression of diverse points of view to enhance teamwork.
Openly share data/findings to support other teams' work.

competencies.competency: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
competencies.description: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect is the commitment to ethical behavior, transparency, and fairness in all professional actions. This competency involves consistently adhering to organizational values, ethical guidelines, and legal standards especially when handling sensitive data or implementing analytical methods. It encompasses identifying, discussing, and mitigating ethical risks, supporting colleagues in ethical decision-making, and ensuring practices such as privacy protection, bias reduction, and inclusion are upheld throughout all processes.
indicators: Comply with the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector in all aspects of data/AI use.
Discuss ethical concerns with appropriate individuals or channels and seek guidance for ethical/privacy issues.
Identify and report ethical concerns when appropriate.
Adhere to the organization's legal, privacy and ethical frameworks (Privacy Act, Policy on Privacy Protection, etc.) and follow disclosure procedures.
Identify and proactively flag privacy/security/accessibility implications.
Consult responsible AI resources.
Consult key policies/procedures on AI for decision-making.
Ensure privacy/security is set at the right permission levels.

competencies.competency: Technical Communication
competencies.description: Technical communication is the ability to effectively convey complex data and analytical insights to diverse audiences, ensuring clarity, accuracy, and relevance. This competency encompasses presenting information using appropriate visual and narrative techniques, adapting messaging to suit stakeholder needs, and linking data findings to organizational objectives. Strong technical communicators make data accessible and actionable, bridging the gap between technical analysis and business decision-making. Mastery of this skill empowers teams to drive informed strategies and foster collaboration across the organization.
indicators: Present basic data analysis results in clear, simple terms using basic charts and graphs (e.g., bar charts, line plots), ensuring key insights are understandable to technical and non-technical audiences.
Summarize the findings of simple analyses (e.g., descriptive statistics or basic trends) in a straightforward manner. Focus on clarity and conciseness.
Use basic visual tools (e.g., Excel charts, basic Python/R plotting) to represent data in ways that make trends and relationships easy to understand.
Use appropriate data/AI terms and concepts when communicating.
Cite sources of information/AI-generated content in visuals.

competencies.competency: Business Acumen

It involves identifying business needs, aligning data-driven insights with organizational goals, and making decisions that drive organizational success.
indicators: Demonstrate basic understanding of key business functions, such as marketing, finance, and operations, and how they relate to data science projects.
Recognize business problems and basic opportunities where data analysis can contribute to business goals.
Understand key financial metrics (e.g., revenue, profit margins, cost structures) and how they impact business decisions.
Present data findings in simple terms, ensuring they are relevant and understandable for business stakeholders.
Recognize various data types and value as an organizational asset.

It encompasses identifying, discussing, and mitigating ethical risks, supporting colleagues in ethical decision-making, and ensuring practices such as privacy protection, bias reduction, and inclusion are upheld throughout all processes.
indicators: Comply with the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector in all aspects of data/AI use.
Discuss ethical concerns with appropriate individuals or channels and seek guidance for ethical/privacy issues.
Identify and report ethical concerns when appropriate.
Adhere to the organization's legal, privacy and ethical frameworks (Privacy Act, Policy on Privacy Protection, etc.) and follow disclosure procedures.
Identify and proactively flag privacy/security/accessibility implications.
Consult responsible AI resources.
Consult key policies/procedures on AI for decision-making.
Ensure privacy/security is set at the right permission levels.

Resolve problems in a sound, logical and decisive manner.

competencies.competency: Technical Communication
competencies.description: Technical communication is the ability to effectively convey complex data and analytical insights to diverse audiences, ensuring clarity, accuracy, and relevance. This competency encompasses presenting information using appropriate visual and narrative techniques, adapting messaging to suit stakeholder needs, and linking data findings to organizational objectives. Strong technical communicators make data accessible and actionable, bridging the gap between technical analysis and business decision-making. Mastery of this skill empowers teams to drive informed strategies and foster collaboration across the organization.
indicators: Present basic data analysis results in clear, simple terms using basic charts and graphs (e.g., bar charts, line plots), ensuring key insights are understandable to technical and non-technical audiences.
Summarize the findings of simple analyses (e.g., descriptive statistics or basic trends) in a straightforward manner. Focus on clarity and conciseness.
Use basic visual tools (e.g., Excel charts, basic Python/R plotting) to represent data in ways that make trends and relationships easy to understand.
Use appropriate data/AI terms and concepts when communicating.
Cite sources of information/AI-generated content in visuals.
